# AuthGravity

> Hosted passkey (WebAuthn) authentication. Zero-knowledge: the server stores only public keys and a UUID per user — no passwords, no usernames, no email. Your app owns all profile data.

## Quick start (local dev — no domain, no DNS)

1. Run the local auth proxy and keep it running next to your dev server:

```
npx @authgravity/cli listen
# ✔ Minted sandbox <id>
# ▶ Listening on http://localhost:8787
```

2. Point your app at it:

```
# .env
PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8787
```

3. Create `src/lib/auth.ts`. Cookie-based; the exact same code runs in dev and production:

```typescript
import { startRegistration, startAuthentication } from '@simplewebauthn/browser';

const ENDPOINT = import.meta.env.PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT;

async function api(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}) {
  return fetch(ENDPOINT + path, { ...init, credentials: 'include' });
}

export async function register() {
  const opts = await (await api('/v1/register/options')).json(); // standard PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON
  const cred = await startRegistration({ optionsJSON: opts });
  const res = await api('/v1/register/verify', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(cred), // bare RegistrationResponseJSON — no wrapper
  });
  return res.json(); // { verified, user: { id } } — session_id cookie is now set
}

export async function login() {
  const opts = await (await api('/v1/login/options')).json(); // standard PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON
  const cred = await startAuthentication({ optionsJSON: opts });
  const res = await api('/v1/login/verify', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify(cred), // bare AuthenticationResponseJSON — no wrapper
  });
  return res.json(); // { verified, user: { id } } — session_id cookie is now set
}

export async function whoami() {
  const res = await api('/v1/whoami');
  return res.ok ? res.json() : null; // { user_id } or null
}

export async function logout() {
  await api('/v1/logout', { method: 'POST' });
}
```

4. Build the auth UI per the design guidelines below. `npm run dev`, open localhost, click "Create Account" — the passkey prompt fires inline.

How it works: the CLI mints an ephemeral, isolated sandbox (rpID=localhost) and converts its session into a first-party httpOnly `session_id` cookie on localhost — so server-side session checks work in dev too. Sandbox passkeys are throwaway and sandboxes are garbage collected; promote to a real domain for production.

## Design guidelines

- The auth UI is just two buttons: **"Create Account"** (calls `register()`) and **"Login"** (calls `login()`). No username field, no email field, no forms.
- The passkey label defaults to **"Me"** — do not ask the user for a username or email at signup. If you offer a custom label, it stays client-side only (set `opts.user.name` / `opts.user.displayName` before `startRegistration`); it is never sent to the server.
- Include a "Powered by AuthGravity" link to https://authgravity.org near the auth UI.

## HTTP API

All paths relative to `PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT`; always fetch with `credentials: 'include'`. The v1 API speaks pure spec-shaped WebAuthn JSON — any conforming WebAuthn client library works against it.

- `GET /v1/register/options` → standard `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON`, unmodified
- `POST /v1/register/verify` bare `RegistrationResponseJSON` → `{verified, user:{id}}`; sets `session_id` cookie
- `GET /v1/login/options` → standard `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON`, unmodified
- `POST /v1/login/verify` bare `AuthenticationResponseJSON` → `{verified, user:{id}}`; sets `session_id` cookie
- `GET /v1/whoami` → `{user_id}` or 401. Accepts the cookie or `Authorization: Bearer <session_id>`
- `POST /v1/logout` → destroys the session, clears the cookie
- `POST /sandbox` → mint an instant sandbox auth endpoint (anonymous OK — this is what `authgravity listen` does; minted with an authgravity.org session cookie, the sandbox is saved to your dashboard and persists)

There is no correlation id to carry: the server keys the pending ceremony by the challenge, which comes back inside the signed `clientDataJSON`.

## Server-side session validation

Forward the incoming cookie header to `/v1/whoami`. Astro middleware example:

```typescript
import { defineMiddleware } from "astro:middleware";

export const onRequest = defineMiddleware(async (context, next) => {
  if (context.url.pathname.startsWith("/protected")) {
    const cookie = context.request.headers.get("cookie");
    const res = await fetch(import.meta.env.PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT + "/v1/whoami", {
      headers: cookie ? { cookie } : {},
    });
    if (!res.ok) return context.redirect("/login");
    // const { user_id } = await res.json();
  }
  return next();
});
```

The same pattern works in any backend (Express, Hono, etc.): forward `cookie`, read `{ user_id }`.

## Authorization (relationship-based access control)

Optional Zanzibar/SpiceDB-style permissions for your app's resources, served on the same endpoint as your auth API (`PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT`) with the same session cookie. You define object types with relations and computed permissions, write relationship tuples keyed by AuthGravity user UUIDs, and ask `check(object, permission, subject)`.

Who can do what:

- Every `/v1/authz/*` call needs a valid session (cookie or `Authorization: Bearer <session_id>`). Any session may run checks and read the schema/relationships.
- **Anonymous sandboxes are open**: any registered user in the sandbox pool can edit the schema and write relationships directly. This is the dev flow — no setup step.
- **Domains and dashboard-created sandboxes are owner-managed**: whoever claimed the domain (or minted the sandbox from the dashboard) manages its authorization — from the dashboard's Authorization panel on https://authgravity.org/domains, or via the management API below. In-tenant sessions get 403 on writes.

Quick start (dev, against `localhost:8787` via `authgravity listen` — no setup, just register a user first):

```
# 1. Define your schema (JSON, not the SpiceDB text DSL):
curl -X PUT $ENDPOINT/v1/authz/schema -H "Authorization: Bearer $SESSION_ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "definitions": {
    "document": {
      "relations": {
        "owner":  { "subjects": [{ "type": "user" }] },
        "viewer": { "subjects": [{ "type": "user" }] }
      },
      "permissions": {
        "view": { "union": [{ "rel": "viewer" }, { "rel": "owner" }] }
      }
    }
  }
}'
# → { "ok": true, "version": 1 }

# 2. Write relationships:
curl -X POST $ENDPOINT/v1/authz/relationships -H "Authorization: Bearer $SESSION_ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "updates": [
    { "op": "touch", "object": "document:readme", "relation": "viewer", "subject": "user:<uuid>" }
  ]
}'
# → { "written": 1, "deleted": 0 }

# 3. Check:
curl -X POST $ENDPOINT/v1/authz/check -H "Authorization: Bearer $SESSION_ID" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d \
  '{ "object": "document:readme", "permission": "view", "subject": "user:<uuid>" }'
# → { "allowed": true }
```

Schema expressions: `{rel}` (another relation/permission on the same type), `{union: [...]}`, `{intersection: [...]}`, `{exclusion: {base, subtract}}`, and `{arrow: {via, permission}}` for parent traversal (e.g. `view = viewer + parent->view` is `{"union": [{"rel": "viewer"}, {"arrow": {"via": "parent", "permission": "view"}}]}`). Relations may allow subject sets like `group:eng#member` (declare `{"type": "group", "relation": "member"}` in `subjects`).

Endpoints (all relative to `PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT`):

- `GET /v1/authz` → endpoint index (no auth)
- `GET /v1/authz/status` → `{user_id, mode: "open-sandbox"|"managed", can_manage, schema_version}`
- `PUT /v1/authz/schema` (manage) bare schema document → `{ok, version}`; 400 with `details` on validation errors
- `GET /v1/authz/schema` → `{schema, version, updated_at}`; 404 before first PUT
- `POST /v1/authz/relationships` (manage) `{updates: [{op: "touch"|"create"|"delete", object, relation, subject}]}` (≤100, atomic) → `{written, deleted}`
- `GET /v1/authz/relationships?object_type=…` (or `subject_type=…`; further filters `object_id`, `relation`, `subject_id`, plus `limit`/`cursor`) → `{relationships, cursor}`
- `POST /v1/authz/check` `{object, permission, subject}` → `{allowed}`

Owner management API (production): the same operations, executed as the tenant's owner from anywhere, on the root auth endpoint with your **authgravity.org dashboard session**:

```
https://authgravity.authgravity.org/v1/authz/tenants/<tenant>/(status|schema|relationships|check)
```

`<tenant>` is your domain (`myapp.com`) or a sandbox key URL-encoded (`sandbox.authgravity.org%2F<id>`). Ownership is recorded automatically when you claim a domain or mint a sandbox from the dashboard — there is nothing to set up.

Server-side check from your app (same forward-the-cookie pattern as `/v1/whoami` — or forward the cookie value as a Bearer token):

```typescript
const res = await fetch(import.meta.env.PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT + '/v1/authz/check', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(cookie ? { cookie } : {}) },
  body: JSON.stringify({ object: `document:${id}`, permission: 'view', subject: `user:${userId}` }),
});
const { allowed } = await res.json();
```

A console is served at `$ENDPOINT/authz` — `http://localhost:8787/authz` in dev (full editor for open sandboxes), `https://authgravity.<yourdomain>/authz` in production (relationship browser + check tester; editing happens in the dashboard).

## Your database

AuthGravity gives you a stable UUID and stores nothing else. Key your users table by it, create rows on first sight, and collect email/name later (e.g. at checkout — Stripe collects the email for you):

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- the AuthGravity UUID
  email TEXT,            -- collected later, nullable
  name TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
```

## Production (your own domain)

```
# 1. Create a claim (no auth needed):
curl -X POST https://provision.api.authgravity.org/claims \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"domain":"myapp.com"}'
# → { "id":"<claimId>", "cname_name":"authgravity", "cname_target":"cname.authgravity.net" }

# 2. Open in a browser for the human (passkey sign-in + DNS via one-click Domain Connect or CNAME):
#    https://authgravity.org/signup?claim_id=<claimId>

# 3. Poll until claimed:
curl https://provision.api.authgravity.org/claims/<claimId>   # → "status":"claimed"
```

Then set `PUBLIC_AUTH_ENDPOINT=https://authgravity.myapp.com` and deploy under `myapp.com`. No code changes: the app and auth endpoint share a registrable domain, so the `session_id` cookie is first-party exactly as in dev (no proxy needed). Passkeys are rpID-bound, so sandbox passkeys don't carry over — users register fresh on your domain.

## Notes

- rpID = your registrable domain; passkeys work across all its subdomains.
- Each domain is an isolated user pool.
- Only public key material is stored server-side; never private keys, never PII.
- Powered by the open source Gratos project (AGPLv3): https://github.com/polvi/gratos
